meta.title: Investigating How All-Trans Retinoic Acid Polycaprolactone (atRA-PCL) Microparticles Alter the Material Properties of 3D Printed Fibrin Constructs.

extracted_by: seed: Claude (Claude Code session), pending human review
summary: All-trans retinoic acid-loaded PCL microparticles were made with microfluidics and mixed into a fibrin bioink printed on a BIO X into an agarose support bath. The study measured how the microparticles change the ink's rheology and drug release.

formulations.crosslinking: chitosan crosslinker (0.075% w/v), printed into 0.5% agarose support bath
formulations.review_notes: The methods sentence swaps units ('pressure ... 11 mm s−1 and the speed to 15 kPa'). Recorded as 15 kPa pressure and 11 mm/s speed; confirm with the authors.
formulations.name: Fibrin bioink + atRA-PCL microparticles (acellular)
formulations.composition_detail: 20 mg/mL fibrinogen, 0.3 mg/mL genipin, 1% w/v alginate
formulations.key_outcome: Microparticles altered the fibrin ink's viscoelastic properties, a material-design step toward built-in neural differentiation cues.

evidence.quote: the final concentration in the bioink was: 20 mg mL−1 fibrinogen, 0.3 mg mL−1 genipin and 1% w/v sodium alginate
For all prints, the pressure was set to 11 mm s−1 and the speed to 15 kPa
3D printing was performed using a BioX 3D printer
